document_title: West Texas A&M's research feedlot and its one AI sentence
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
USDA is paying for half of a research feedlot near Canyon.

The A&M System calls the $9.75 million grant to West Texas A&M the largest federal award in WT's history. A dollar-for-dollar match from the System, the Texas Cattle Feeders Association, donors and other sources brings the project to $19.5 million.

The feedlot will pair 90 small research pens with 45 commercial-scale pens. Ground was broken in November 2025 next to WT's Nance Ranch.

On September 1st USDA estimated 2.5 million cattle on feed in Texas's large feedlots. Nebraska and Kansas each had fewer.

The release mentions AI once. New techniques "can be evaluated" with traditional and AI-powered approaches. It names no AI tool, vendor, camera, model or result.

If AI is tested in these pens, will WT's Feedlot Research Group name the tool and report the result?

#WestTexasAM #CanyonTX #TexasPanhandle

S2.headline: USDA pays half. The match pays the rest.
S2.body: A required dollar for dollar match brings the project to $19.5 million. The A&M System puts in $4.875 million. The Texas Cattle Feeders Association, donors and other sources match it. Each section is drawn to stand for one $4.875 million share.

S3.headline: The feedlot goes up beside WT's 2,393-acre ranch
S3.body: The ranch lies about seven miles east of Canyon and was given to WT in 1971. Canyon ranchers Mike and Gary Kuhlman gave 42.84 acres beside it in 2024. Each is drawn as a square of its own area, not its real shape or exact place.

S4.headline: 90 research pens paired with 45 commercial ones
S4.body: That is 135 pens in all. Each commercial-scale pen here faces two small research pens across a feed alley. The layout and pen sizes are drawn to illustrate the count.

S5.headline: Ground is broken. Four facilities are planned.
S5.body: Ground was broken in November 2025. Plans call for a precision beef cattle handling facility, a veterinary care and research hospital, an advanced technology feed and production center and a metabolism and physiology center. The section and stakes are drawn to illustrate.
strings: Ground is broken. Four facilities are planned.

S6.headline: Texas's large feedlots held more cattle than Nebraska's or Kansas's
S6.body: On September 1st USDA estimated 2.5 million cattle on feed in Texas's large feedlots, 2.47 million in Nebraska and 2.32 million in Kansas. Texas held 22 percent of the 11.16 million nationwide. Each steer is drawn to stand for 500 thousand head.

S7.headline: The release mentions AI once
S7.body: The mention is a planned way of evaluating techniques. The page is drawn to illustrate. The words are the release's own.

New feeding, health and handling techniques can be evaluated with traditional and artificial intelligence-powered approaches that are designed to increase beef production efficiency and advance feedlot management practices.
